newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Publisher Epiphania goes public July 8-10.
newsitem.headline: Greek Publisher Epiphania goes public July 8-10.

text.p: Epiphania SA, a specialist in business publications and print communications, is going public on July 8-10 and will be a new listing on the bourse's small-cap parallel market.
Epiphania which designs and produces smart, upmarket business publications, is also also active in multimedia and electronic marketing.
It will tap the capital market for 560 million drachmas with a public offering of 350,000 common bearer shares at 1,600 drachmas a share -- 9.7 times its 1996 pretax earnings.
The company will also privately place 17,500 shares bringing total proceeds to 588 million drachmas. Its total outstanding shares after the IPO will be 2,367,500 shares.
Lead underwriter and issue advisor is Telesis Securities joined by co-underwriters National Bank Eurobank, Xiosbank, Alpha Brokerage, NIBID and N. Devletoglou Securities.
In 1996 Epiphania had sales of 1.64 billion drachmas and pretax profit of 289 million. It projects sales of 1.8 billion this year and pretax earnings of 330 million.
It sees sales in the first half of this year advancing 15 percent and contributing to a 20 percent growth in earnings.
Epiphania is managed by main shareholders Theodore Kaloudis and Thanasis Panagoulias with equal 36.3 percent stakes. Venture capital firm Baring Hellenic Ventures has a 17.4 percent stake.
Kaloudis, a former journalist, has held many posts as a correspondent and chief editor for dailies Eleftherotypia, Kerdos, Ethnos and was recently the publisher of financial daily Imerisia.
Panagoulias, formerly an art director with Olympic DDB Needham was also the creative manager for magazines Playboy, Car & Driver and Elle, published by Athenian Publications.

Epiphania SA has handled the corporate communications of a number of Athens bourse listings including OTE telecom, Goody's, Hellas Can and handles publications for Citibank, Diners Club, Interamerican, Lavipharm and Hellenic Bottling.
It also designed and runs the recent Greek publication of Tempo-Newsweek magazine. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
